title: Slow-cooker chicken cassoulet
subtitle: A simplified French cassoulet for the slow cooker
excerpt: Chicken thighs and smoked sausage braised with haricot beans, tomatoes, and herbs. A relaxed take on the great French bean stew that suits a weeknight as well as a Sunday.
sourceNotes: Cassoulet is a slow-cooked casserole originating in the Languedoc region of France, documented in detail by Elizabeth David, French Provincial Cooking (1960). This version uses chicken thighs and smoked sausage in place of duck confit and Toulouse sausage.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat gently on the hob.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The flavour improves overnight. Make the day before and reheat gently.

content.text: Proper cassoulet takes two days and an argument. This version is built for a slow cooker on a weekday and still produces something worth eating. Chicken thighs replace duck confit, smoked sausage replaces Toulouse, and the haricot beans remain non-negotiable. The slow cooker does the rest.
The smoked sausage is key to the depth of flavour. Kielbasa or any smoked pork sausage works well. Slice it thickly so it holds its shape during the long cook.
Serve in deep bowls with crusty bread. A fresh green salad cuts through the richness.

Spread {{haricot-beans}} of haricot beans in the base of the slow cooker. Place {{chicken-thighs-boneless}} of chicken thighs on top. Tuck in {{smoked-pork-sausage}} of sliced smoked sausage. Add {{onion}} diced onion and {{garlic}} of crushed garlic. Pour over {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes, {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree, and {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock. Add {{thyme}} of thyme and {{bay-leaves}} of bay. Season with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt.
Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 7 to 8 hours. The chicken should be very tender. Discard the thyme and bay leaves. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve in deep bowls.

rows.symptom: The beans have turned to mush
rows.cause: Tinned beans become very soft after 8 hours on LOW.
rows.fix: Add the beans in the last 2 hours only next time. This keeps them tender but still holding their shape.

rows.cause: The tomatoes and stock released more liquid than the beans absorbed.
rows.fix: Remove the lid and set to HIGH for 30 minutes. The sauce will reduce and thicken. Alternatively, remove some of the beans and mash them, then stir back in.

rows.cause: A very long cook can break down some smoked sausages, especially lower-quality ones.
rows.fix: Add the sliced sausage in the last hour only next time. It only needs to heat through.

rows.cause: The smoked sausage lacked smokiness, or the herbs were dried rather than fresh.
rows.fix: Add a pinch of smoked paprika. A teaspoon of Worcestershire sauce also deepens the flavour.

content.text: Cassoulet is one of the most debated dishes in French cooking. The three towns of Castelnaudary, Carcassonne, and Toulouse each claim to make the definitive version. All agree on one thing: it must be slow-cooked and it must contain white beans. This version is a straightforward simplification that captures the spirit of the original.
